subject.title: [Feature]: Add $EDITOR compose mode in TUI (external editor handoff) for multiline prompts

question: Should OpenClaw add a core TUI VISUAL/EDITOR compose handoff now, and what trigger plus privacy/process guardrails should govern it?
rationale: The feature is coherent and still missing, but it executes a user-selected local process and persists prompt contents outside the in-memory composer, so automation should not choose the UX or security boundary alone.

options.title: Approve bounded core flow
options.body: Implement a chosen shortcut or slash command that suspends the TUI, round-trips the draft through VISUAL then EDITOR, never auto-submits, documents privacy/error behavior, and adds focused tests.

options.title: Require design first
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers settle shortcut conflicts, slash-command discoverability, temp-file lifetime, and privacy wording.

options.title: Defer editor handoff
options.body: Leave long-prompt ergonomics to inline multiline behavior or other composer improvements and decline external editor process launch for now.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded core flow
recommendation.body: Implement a chosen shortcut or slash command that suspends the TUI, round-trips the draft through VISUAL then EDITOR, never auto-submits, documents privacy/error behavior, and adds focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined signal from the prior issue review, TUI editor history, and current-line ownership in this area.
